text:
Priya: Quick heads-up — seeing intermittent packet loss (0.5-2%) on overlay between GPU pods during scheduled backfills. Pattern looks like short sawtooth spikes ~20-40s recurring every ~3-6min. Only in us-east-2a so far.
Marco: Noticed similar in the tail latencies earlier, thought it was gRPC retries. Any pcap or tcpdump yet?
Priya: grabbed a tcpdump on host eth0 and on the pod veth. Host -> overlay shows small bursts of retransmits. Pod-side looks fine for a bit then drops.
Aisha: Can you paste the tcpdump snippet? also which encap — vxlan or geneve?
Priya: geneve on this cluster. snippet: ```
14:12:03.123456 IP podA > podB: Flags [P.], seq 123:456, ack 789, win 65535
14:12:03.127890 IP podA > podB: Flags [.], ack 456, win 65535 (retransmission)
```
Ken: Any MTU diffs? offload toggles? We've seen GSO/GRO/GRO/LSO interactions cause weird reassembly on some mlx5 drivers.
Priya: MTU is 1450 on host, 1420 inside geneve (accounting for overhead). Offloads were enabled. I tried disabling tx-udp-seg, didn't change much.
Tyrone: Did you check underlay drops / NIC counters? On mlx5 sometimes caused by hardware LRO/GRO heuristics when packets come in bursts.
Priya: host ethtool -S shows small increment in tx_queue_drops on one NIC during spike windows.
Marco: That matches. Also correlate with kube-scheduler backfill events? Backfills are causing short bursty fanout across nodes when restarting GPU pods.
Aisha: Are we seeing this on Dedicated clusters only or hosted too?
Priya: Only Dedicated us-east-2a (gpu-pool-3). No reports from other regions.
SRE-Bot: [deploy] backfill job gpu-backfill-2026-03-18 triggered at 14:10:40; target nodes: 24.
Marco: There — large fanout at job start. Could be many small TCP flows saturating queue and exposing offload edgecases.
Ken: Suggest next steps: 1) schedule small controlled backfill on canary nodes and capture NIC counters/flow-level metrics; 2) toggle GSO/GRO on one node to compare; 3) measure iperf/udp vs tcp; 4) enable per-encap checksum offload diagnostics.
Priya: Doing a quick canary now on gpu-pool-canary-1 (isolated AZ). Running: ```kubectl run -i --rm loadgen --image=networkstatic/iperf3 -- iperf3 -c podB -P 16 -t 60```
Tyrone: Also add `tcpdump -n -w /tmp/host.pcap 'udp or tcp'` on the host and `tcpdump -n -w /tmp/pod.pcap` in the pod netns.
Aisha: If we confirm it's related to bursty flow fanout, a mitigation could be to stagger pod restarts in backfill or reduce parallelism. Long-term: tune NIC driver params or offload heuristics for ML fleet patterns.
Priya: Canary run: small loss spike at 14:25, counters: tx_queue_drops +42 on nic1, softirq CPU spike on that host.
Ken: Softirq spike suggests CPU-side processing bottleneck; check interrupt affinity / RSS. Are IRQs pinned to same core as the GPU tasks?
Priya: Good call — IRQs are on default distribution. I'll try isolating IRQs to dedicated cores and re-run.
Marco: Also check kernel ring sizes: `ethtool -G <if> rx 4096 tx 4096` and `sysctl net.core.rmem_max` etc.
Priya: Update: after increasing ring sizes and moving IRQs, saw reduction in packet loss spikes (down to ~0.2% and shorter). Will run more iterations.
Tyrone: If this holds, create a runbook: detection (softirq + tx_queue_drops during backfill), quick mitigation (stagger backfills, increase ring, pin IRQs), and long term (driver/kernel tune + evaluate disabling GSO on vulnerable NICs).
Priya: Agree. I'll file a KB and schedule follow-up to test on more nodes/azs. Thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
SRE-Bot: [note] Created incident draft: encap-sawtooth-loss-us-east-2a (priority P2)
Priya: Pls add the tcpdump pcaps to the incident and link to gpu-backfill job logs.
Marco: Also add kubelet event timeseries so we can align pod churn with spikes.
Priya: Will do.
